title: Freelance work in early television and radio
summary: On the strength of the Hit Parade, Leeman is hired as a freelance on the Perry Como, Jack Benny, Steve Allen and Telephone Hour shows, and works on 'You Are There' with Louis Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: However -- at this time, I was in to the Hit Parade, which I did on weekends, and my reputation was growing there. I was fortunate to be able to read and cut a few parts, and I was hired by contractors, I had a reputation of working on the Hit Parade, which was a great show in those days -- I was hired, I ws what you'd call on the 'outside'. A freelance artist. But I was still working nights until four o'clock in the morning, which was killing at times.

And from the Hit Parade show, I would sub on the Perry Como Show and I did the Jack Benny Show -- these were all outside things -- the Jimmy Durante Show, these were all the beginning of television; television was just coming in strong then, and I was in on the ground floor. I did the Telephone Hour with Red Nichols, and I also did the Telephone Hour as a musician -- they hired me to keep time with several

of the modern features they did on those shows. I did the Steve Allen Tonight Show, and I did a great show that featured Louis Armstrong on CBS -- You Are There Show, and one of the titles was The Closing of Storyville, and that was a great feather in my bonnet. Louis Armstrong, Bobby Hackett -- I was with the Lawson-Haggard Band, and we emulated the original Dixieland -- the Original Dixieland Jazz Band was the name of it.

That You Are There Show as done by the great Walter Cronkite, and also -- I don't know whether I mentioned Jack Teagarden, but he was in that. I did thousands of commercial jingles and free lance pop records, with all the top stars of the era. Thirty-one jazz albums with the Lawson-Haggard band, which I will get to as a separate piece, because that was one of the highlights of my life.

And I did a series of Billy Butterfield albums -- and we'll list these later on if anybody's interested, I can't get into the research now. Bob Crosby albums, especially South Pacific and Porgy and Bess -- those are collector's items now, and I'd recommend anybody that wants to hear a powerful type of music.
